title: lake build repeatedly hit "build lock timeout" despite long tool timeouts, then succeeded
body: Called `lake build Rule30.Proofs.BoolXorDrivenPeriodicFrom` 7 times in a row (some with a 590000ms Bash tool timeout) and each returned near-instantly with the bare string "build lock timeout" -- far faster than the 590s I allowed, suggesting the lock-wait timeout inside the guard/build wrapper is much shorter than the caller's timeout and is not configurable from the worker side. `lake env lean Rule30/Proofs/BoolXorDrivenPeriodicFrom.lean` succeeded cleanly in between attempt 6 and 7 with no output, and then the 8th `lake build` attempt succeeded normally in 1.7s. This cost 7 wasted turns waiting on lock contention with no way to see queue position or force a longer wait. Not fatal since it eventually cleared, but worth checking whether the internal lock-wait is shorter than intended given `run --concurrency 3` is the documented normal load.
